key_insight: ActMOF turns sparse, noisy MOF synthesis data into an experiment-grounded benchmark that shows Gaussian-process active learning is a top choice for mapping crystallization landscapes.
engineering_relevance: The framework helps materials engineers choose and compare search strategies before running expensive synthesis campaigns, improving efficiency in reticular MOF discovery.
method: Built a benchmark from experimentally measured microwave syntheses of aluminum-carboxylate MOFs.
Encoded each condition with a crystallinity index derived from diffraction peak intensity and full width at half-maximum.
Compared active-learning policies using Gaussian processes, tree ensembles, and large language models, then validated transfer on six related MOFs.
evidence_signal: The benchmark evaluation placed the GP family among the leading policies, and six transfer campaigns produced crystalline products within a fixed budget of 12 experiments each.
watch_item: Because the benchmark is based on sparse microwave synthesis data with noisy crystallization outcomes, performance may depend strongly on the specific chemistry and measurement protocol.
paper_title: ActMOF: Mapping Reticular Synthesis through Active Learning
